source.title: Cross-seed explainability using Procrustes-conditioned Joint End-to-end Top-K Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-seed feature correlations and universality using SAE-based methods, rather than testing convergence with the original studies’ methods. It tests feature alignment across independently initialized models, not convergence with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cross-seed SAE feature correlations and universal-feature counts across three datasets and several alignment/training conditions. It also reports a mean-pooling evaluation in Appendix C. The reported residual/alignment analyses and random-rotation comparisons in Appendices B and D are not included as rows because the 60-row limit is reached by the main table and the pooling comparison. Claims about other studies in the text are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: Independently fitted, Hungarian-matched SAEs measure shared features across BERT seeds without a cross-seed training penalty. Joint-training ablations without that penalty provide additional evidence, although they use a shared extractor. The full pipeline directly optimizes sparse-code agreement, so its performance cannot independently establish spontaneous convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors present Procrustes-conditioned joint Top-K SAEs as a promising method for extracting correlated cross-seed features, with rotation most useful during joint training. They acknowledge testing only one BERT family and lacking direct comparisons with other aligned SAE methods. Their single-feature interpretation is preliminary, and the full pipeline's explicit agreement loss prevents treating its correlations alone as independent evidence of natural universality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Procrustes-conditioned joint SAE, Top-K sparsity, end-to-end losses and cross-seed feature correlation evaluation; it is not a reproduction of either named original source. It jointly trains a feature extractor after independently training BERT seeds.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across datasets, SAE training/alignment conditions, and pooling choice. Post-hoc rotation of independent SAEs does not reliably improve feature correlation; rotation during joint training does better in the reported comparisons. Sentence-level mean pooling changes results relative to per-token evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: The full pipeline increases correlations and threshold-defined universal shares while explicitly minimizing cross-seed sparse-code discrepancies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Procrustes-conditioned joint SAE training can produce more correlated extracted codes than post-hoc matching.

fits_no_version.finding: Edits to sentence-initial modals reduce the activation of Politeness feature 389, but the study does not demonstrate the same interpretation separately across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An extracted SAE feature responds to sentence-initial modal interrogatives.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE injection leaves classification accuracy approximately unchanged; each model receives its own reconstructed activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SAE reconstruction preserves classification performance in the tested models.

record.problems: Only one BERT model family is tested, with five seed pairs in the main results and two seed pairs in Appendix C. The study does not test scale or capability. Universal-feature counts rely on a chosen Pearson-r threshold and the paper notes that mean pooling can introduce noise. Cross-seed alignment is assessed after specialized SAE alignment/training, so it does not show that the underlying independently trained models naturally converge without that procedure.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the Top-10 and other condition rows from Appendix C3, the rotation-distance/sample-size validation in Appendix B, and the identity, mismatched-correspondence and random-rotation counts in Appendix D, including its pair-level values. The included rows prioritize the complete Table 1 correlation/universality measures and the Appendix C3 full-pipeline pooling comparison.

untested.parts: No size or capability sweep, or comparison across architectures, training objectives or training data.

No broad architecture replication or demonstration that shared structure spans the whole representation. The text is ambiguous about random initialization versus fine-tuning a common pretrained BERT checkpoint.
No transfer of one model's representations into the other with measured task retention. Within-model SAE reconstruction and geometric Procrustes alignment do not establish interchangeability.

The single interpreted feature is not separately interpreted and causally checked in both seeds. Correlation-defined universality does not establish recurrence of the same interpretable feature or circuit.

No alternative similarity metric, neighbour-count sweep, threshold sweep or out-of-distribution evaluation. Pooling comparisons do not isolate pooling from seed-pair aggregation and possible setup changes.
No scale-dependent plateau or causal comparison separating shared data and objectives from other explanations of alignment.

missing.what: Absolute universal-feature counts and dead-feature fractions accompanying the percentages. For independent matched SAEs these are 236±124 and 56.5±14.1% dead on Politeness, 23±12 and 81.9±3.4% on SST-2, and 81±19 and 73.6±0.8% on TweetEval. These contextualize the restricted active-in-both denominator.

Clarification of base-model initialization: Section 3.2 states random initialization, while Appendix A calls the procedure fine-tuning and names bert-base-uncased. Whether seeds share pretrained weights materially affects the independence interpretation.
missing.locator: Section 3.2 and Appendix A, Table A1

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Main-table numerical values are correctly transcribed. Raw-index nulls do not challenge V3, which explicitly allows different units and bases. For V6-linked index and matched rows, states describe measured agreement within each condition; their contrast supplies the metric-dependence evidence. Partial alignment is positive evidence for V7's incompleteness component. Joint ablations without cross-code loss are retained as conditional extraction evidence, whereas full-pipeline correlations directly optimize agreement. Appendix B and D results and omitted Appendix C conditions are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. No verdict relies on those omitted results.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no comparison across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.

Tests feature correlations and shared feature counts for same-family BERT models across seeds, with SAE alignment/training procedures. Does not establish that unmodified networks spontaneously learn the same individual units or bases.

Uses Procrustes rotation to condition SAE training, but does not test transferability by stitching layers, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or a direct low-loss representation interchangeability test.

Measures recurring SAE features by cross-seed activation correlation and gives a minimal qualitative analysis of one feature; it does not systematically compare interpreted features or circuits across models.
Compares per-token with sentence-level mean-pooling evaluation and reports results on three datasets. Does not systematically vary neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports incomplete cross-seed feature universality and tests models from one BERT family using the same datasets. It does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, nor test a scale-dependent plateau.
